findings.message: This is an instance fix: only the extend job locks the standing row. In `setStanding`, the delete of standing-written month rows runs before the `update allocations.standing ...`, and that update is the first statement to lock the row. `skipMonths` has the same problem: its caller deletes the month rows first, then updates `skip`. Under READ COMMITTED the delete runs on a snapshot that can't see rows the extend job has inserted but not yet committed. The delete then waits on the extend's lock and does not delete those rows once the extend commits. The previous round also asked for a test that runs the two writers at the same time, and none was added (B7). Fix: in both writers, lock the open standing row first with `select ... for update`, then delete and update. Add a test that runs `extendStanding` and an end (and a hand removal) in two real sessions at once, and that fails without the lock.
findings.scenario: Dinesh stands on CON at 50% with filled_to 2027-09. The extend tx locks the standing row and inserts 2027-10 and 2027-11 (not committed yet). At the same time, allocate {standing:true, month:'2027-09', percent:0} deletes the standing rows from 2027-09 on. It sees only committed rows, then waits on the update. The extend commits, and the end then sets until_month=2027-09. Result: 2027-10 and 2027-11 stay at 50% after the standing ended. The same thing happens when a hand removal of 2027-11 races the extend: the skip is recorded but the 50% row exists.

findings.message: `personNamed` is a second copy of the service's `personOf` (services.ts:27). The two disagree on an ambiguous name: `personOf` refuses with 'matches more than one person; use the employee number', but `personNamed` returns null. `proposeAllocate` then reports the person as missing from HR, and it may even tell the PM to add them to HR, which creates a duplicate person. Fix: use one resolver that returns found / ambiguous / none, and have `proposeAllocate` surface 'use the employee number' when the name is ambiguous.
findings.scenario: Two active HR people are called 'Kasun Perera', and one of them has a sign-in. 'Add Kasun Perera to CON' is refused before the card with 'Kasun Perera can sign in but has no HR record yet. Add them to HR first: "add Kasun Perera to HR for CON"'. Following it creates a third Kasun Perera record.

findings.message: This is an instance fix. The 'links to X's sign-in' note is worked out once, from the work email the card was built with. But `workEmail` is an editable text field on the same card, and the edit check (FormConfirm `onCheck`) never rebuilds the title. If someone types or changes the email on the card, the new record still links silently to whatever active account has that email. `linksTo` is also a second copy of the link rule in addPerson's insert subquery (services.ts:56). Fix: have the edit check return the link as a notice from the edited `workEmail` (or show it on the button label through the form). Derive both the card and the service from one shared 'account this email links to' function.
findings.scenario: The model opens 'Add Ravi to HR' with no email, so the title has no link note. On the card the person types the work email sahan@lumenlabs.test, which belongs to an active account with no HR record, and confirms. The new HR record is linked to Sahan's sign-in, and nothing on the card ever said so.

findings.message: The standing path's audit `before` now lists the month rows it deleted, but not the standing rows it ends or deletes (`setStanding` lines 36–37). Those rows hold their percent, from_month and the new `skip` list, so a mistaken re-set loses the removals by hand with no trace of them in the audit. Add the ended or deleted standing rows to `before`.
